title: A sharp stop-loss bound for Rademacher sums, the constant two in a concave comparison, and local extremal sets on the discrete cube
shortTitle: Two equal coins: a sharp Rademacher stop-loss bound
oneLine: Kontorovich's concave comparison holds with constant 2, and what this says about sets of large first-level weight on the cube
abstract: Flip fair coins, attach weights whose squares sum to one, and add the signed weights. How much of this Rademacher sum lies, on average, more than one standard deviation from zero? Answering a question Kontorovich asked on MathOverflow, Lowther reduced it to whether the mean excess E(|S| − 1)₊ is at most (√2 − 1)/2, the value for two equal coins, and proved a weaker constant. This candidate proves the sharp bound, E(|S| − t)₊ ≤ (√2 − t)/2 for every threshold t in [1/√2, 1.005], with equality only for two equal weights and a quadratic stability estimate. Hence for independent symmetric random variables and increasing concave f with f(0) = 0, the expectation of f at the square function is at most twice its expectation at the absolute sum; the constant 2 is sharp and extends to sign-invariant vectors in Hilbert space with linear stability, and Kontorovich's constant for tensorizing total variation improves from 0.1798 to (1 − e^(−1/2))/2 ≈ 0.1967. An inequality of Fang and Huang for three coefficients is extended to all weights. On the discrete cube, sets of density 1/4 ± h with maximal first-level weight are shown, unconditionally, to gain (2 + o(1))h² log(1/h). Assuming a theorem from Lei Yu's unrefereed 2026 preprint, the paper gives an exact formula near 1/4, the next-order terms and a 0.979 : 0.021 split of added mass between two faces governed by a Curie–Weiss–Potts equation, and the analogue near density 1/8. Limits: the thresholds are proved only on [1/√2, 1.005]; the cube results are local with non-explicit neighbourhoods; the finer cube results rely on Yu's preprint; density 1/16 is open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: An 18-page paper with a context-first introduction, written proofs, limits, open problems and an AI-use statement. Four Python programs accompany it, each failing on error under python -O: verify.py checks the stop-loss bound exactly at four thresholds, the three-coin bound for 1,000 integer weight tuples and an enclosure for 923 planar vector tuples; cube_census.py checks all 65,536 subsets of the four-dimensional cube and computes the constants to 80 digits; verify_asymptotic.py is a floating-point illustration of the asymptotic constants; check_extensions.py evaluates proof margins, interval endpoints, constants and the evidence for the conjecture. A clean replay in optimised mode reproduced the recorded outputs byte for byte; changing one census mass makes cube_census.py fail; Linux CI reruns the three quick scripts and compares floating-point lines with a declared tolerance.

keyResults: Theorem 3.1 (proof): for unit weights and every t in [1/√2, 201/200], E(|S| − t)₊ ≤ (√2 − t)/2, with equality only for two equal weights, and a quadratic stability estimate at t = 1; this is Lowther's proposed bound. Proposition 3.3: two equal coins are not optimal outside [2 − √2, 2√2 − √3]; Conjecture 10.1 asks for that whole interval.
Corollary 4.1 and Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 (proof): Kontorovich's concave comparison holds with the sharp constant 2, also for sign-invariant vectors in Hilbert space, with linear stability.
Corollary 4.5 (proof): Kontorovich's total-variation tensorization constant improves from 0.1798 to (1 − e^(−1/2))/2 ≈ 0.1967.
Theorem 6.1 (proof): Fang and Huang's capped three-coefficient inequality holds for all coefficients, with stability.
Proposition 7.1 and Theorem 7.2 (proof, unconditional): W(1/4 ± h) = 2 min(1/4, 1/4 ± h)² + (2 + o(1)) h² log(1/h) for the dimension-free maximal first-level weight.

Corollaries 7.3 and 8.2 and Theorems 7.4 and 8.1 (proof conditional on Theorem 5 of Lei Yu's unrefereed September 2026 preprint): exact formula near density 1/4, next-order terms, a 0.979 : 0.021 split of added mass between two faces, and the analogue near density 1/8.

Credit and limits: Kontorovich (question and TV application), Lowther (reduction and proposed bound), Yu (Theorem 5, used for the finer results), Fang and Huang (capped lemma, majorant, density-1/8 value). Thresholds proved only on [1/√2, 1.005]; cube results local; density 1/16 open.
